notes:
S1 disabled (engine=strategy2.py). 2026-08-27 session: NO PARAMETER CHANGES. One live incident, one correction to last night's own recommendation, two tools built.

1. LIVE INCIDENT -- THE BOT WAS BLIND AND NOTHING SAID SO. At 02:00 UTC the last completed candle scan was 00:01. Every Hyperliquid call had been timing out for two hours: 257 ConnectTimeout warnings, 50 Cycle errors. Cause is EXTERNAL and confirmed independently of the bot -- DNS resolves fine, Telegram and 1.1.1.1 connect in 0.16s, but every one of the 8 A-records behind api.hyperliquid.xyz and api.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz sits in 99.86.171.0/24, and raw TCP to that entire /24 times out. One CloudFront edge PoP unreachable from this host; mainnet and testnet share it, so there is no failover to reach. Book was flat, no capital at risk.

WHAT THE INCIDENT EXPOSED is a third liveness failure mode that NEITHER existing guard covers. _watchdog() checks _last_tick and the loop was ticking normally -- it cycles, raises, sleeps, repeats. .heartbeat checks host death and was fresh to the second. systemd said active (running). All three health signals read green while the bot had not seen a price in two hours. get_positions() raises at the top of the cycle, before the candle check is ever reached, so no scan completes and nothing measures that. tg.send_error() does fire, but dedups to 'upstream gateway error x25 in the last 30 min', which reads as transient noise rather than 'you are blind'.

FIXED: live.py now tracks _last_scan_ok, set only on reaching the end of a full candle pass (every earlier exit is a continue, every failure an exception, so this is the one signal that separates 'cycling' from 'looking at the market'). _check_scan_stale() runs in the existing watchdog thread and DMs once per episode if no scan completes in SCAN_STALE_ALERT_SEC=8100 (2h15m: needs two consecutive misses, and clears the nightly review's ~1h10m legitimate scan-free stretch). Quiet hours 02:00-04:00 suppressed. Names any open position and warns the ratchet cannot arm. Sends a recovery DM when scanning resumes. DELIBERATELY DOES NOT RESTART -- a restart cannot reach a dead API, and the trade-restore block needs get_positions() to succeed; when it does not, _open_trades stays permanently empty and any open position is orphaned from the bot's own exit management for the life of that process. Alerting is strictly better than restarting here. New test_scan_stale.py, 15 assertions, all pass.

2. CORRECTION TO LAST NIGHT'S CAP ANALYSIS -- IT FLIPS THE RECOMMENDATION. The 2026-08-26 note says that under a 0.3% cap ETH 'would have been capped at roughly +2.40R instead of +2.17R', implying ~+0.23R of free money from narrowing RATCHET_SLIP_CAP. That is wrong, and the same note contradicts it two sentences later: a Hyperliquid trigger with isMarket:True fires an IOC whose unfilled remainder is CANCELLED, not rested. An order that cannot fill inside its cap does not fill at a worse-but-capped price -- it does not fill AT ALL. ETH's adverse fill was 1.047% of price, so at a 0.30% cap that stop would simply not have executed, and update_sl cancels the old stop AND the TP before placing the new one. The trade is not '+0.23R for free'; it is 0.33R against leaving an unprotected short mid-move. RECOMMENDATION TO KAMRAN: do NOT narrow RATCHET_SLIP_CAP to 0.30%. If it is touched at all, 1.25-1.50% still covers every observed fill with headroom while trimming the tail -- but there is no measured case it would have helped, so the honest answer is leave it at 2.00%. Values unchanged; this is an owner call either way.

WHY THE ERROR WAS INVISIBLE: the report measured the leak only in R. R is right for edge (it normalises across coins) and wrong for an execution cap, which is enforced as a fraction of price -- and R/entry differs 3.6x across these three trades (SOL 0.81%, SUI 1.30%, ETH 2.93%). The old line said the worst fill 'sits inside the 2.00% cap' without ever printing what it was, which invites exactly the wrong inference. analyze._ratchet_slippage now computes adv_pct per arm and the section prints the fill vs trigger in percent, the worst fill as a share of the cap, and an explicit warning naming any arm that a tightened cap would have failed to fill.

3. THE LEAK IS ONE BAD FILL, NOT A BROAD TAX. Added a concentration line: ETH 2026-08-21 alone is 80% of the total 0.414R leak. Per-arm adverse fills are SOL 0.019%, SUI 0.074%, ETH 1.047% -- the two longs cost essentially nothing (1.0% and 3.7% of their locks), the one SHORT cost 14x the worst long. A mean over three arms hid that, and 'broad tax' and 'one bad fill' have different fixes. Hypothesis worth watching, n=1 so NOT acted on: a short's ratchet stop is a BUY, and buying into a squeeze is where slippage lives. If the next 2-3 short arms also fill >0.5% adverse while longs stay under 0.1%, that is a direction-conditional execution problem and a real finding. Until then it is one trade.

NOT CHANGED and why: no S2 constant -- all owner-locked, and the book is n=17, WR 41.2%, sumR +2.61, EV +0.153R, t=+0.42, still not distinguishable from a coin flip. No S1 numeric -- S1 is disabled, so tuning min_score/trail_pct/min_adx/session is theatre. apply_config_to_trader() not run: no S1 value moved and it rewrites trader.py for nothing. WATCHLIST not touched despite DOGE 20.5% / ATOM 16.3% / OP 15.2% / ARB 14.2% / WLD 11.9% frozen bars -- owner-locked, and the gate-contamination check is reassuring anyway: 0/854 signals qualified on a frozen bar vs 45/8485 on live ones, because a frozen price cannot print a NEW extreme. Staleness suppresses signals rather than faking them, so it costs frequency, not accuracy.

HEALTH. test_ratchet 11/11 including the live-state-untouched lock; test_exit_price 5/5; test_scan_stale 15/15. state.json untouched (mtime 00:30, predates this session). PROCESS NOTE: test_scan_stale wrote 4 phantom ERROR lines into the live bot.log on its first run, because importing live.py attaches a loguru sink to bot.log at module scope. Removed them in place (open r+/truncate, NOT sed -i -- the running bot holds that file open and replacing the inode would send every later log line to an unlinked file), and the test now calls logger.remove() before doing anything. Same class as the 2026-08-24 suite that corrupted live state.
